_comment: What we have actually run, not what we recommend. Models age in weeks and this file is
fetched at runtime for that reason: a name compiled into the installer would still be
advertised long after it stopped being a sensible choice, and the installer does not
update itself.
Rules for adding a line here:
- only models someone on the project has actually run the instruction suite against
- 'note' says what was observed, in one sentence, with no superlative
- never a ranking: the suite is a heuristic on free text and the machine matters as much
as the model. The person testing decides; this only tells them where to start.
- NEVER pick or rank by language. Sorting by 'good at Japanese' would break the rule the
whole project is built on: every part of it stays language-agnostic.
'pull' is what makes a model offerable for download. An entry without it is a note only —
which is right for a family name like 'gemma' that matches many things, and for anything we
would not put in front of someone as a starting point.
TAGS ARE PINNED TO A VERSION, NEVER 'latest'. A moving tag makes every figure below a lie
the day it moves, and the reader has no way of knowing which day that was.
'min_vram_gb' is the card size below which the model runs on the processor instead, which
means minutes per line rather than seconds. It filters the offer; it never hides the list.
⚠ It is NOT the download size, and the two differ wildly in BOTH directions: gemma4:e4b
downloads 9.6 GB and holds 3.2 in memory, qwen3:8b downloads 5.2 GB and takes 9.3. Every
figure here is the model tester's own reading, plus a gigabyte of headroom, rounded up to a
card size that exists. Where a note quotes memory, that is the raw measurement.
⚠ THESE MODELS ARE SAMPLED, NOT DETERMINISTIC. The tester now judges four answers instead of
one, because a single draw is worth very little: translategemma:12b passes the whole suite
and still dropped a placeholder on one draw in four. One bad line in four corrupts a game's
text quietly, which is worse than a model that fails openly — so a note says how many draws
held, never 'reliable'.
'languages' is the PUBLISHER'S claim, never our measurement — we have verified none of them.
Two numbers when they give two: a model tuned for 35 languages that merely saw 140 in
training is not the same promise, and the difference matters to whoever falls in the gap.
⚠ It stays a COUNT. Recording WHICH languages, and filtering the offer by what somebody is
translating into, is the one thing this project does nowhere.

models.note: What the mod is developed against. Follows the instruction suite in full, including the experimental source-language rule, and kept every placeholder across four draws. Held 6.1 GB of video memory here.

Passed the whole suite and kept every placeholder across four draws while holding 1.7 GB of video memory — the smallest footprint anything here has managed, and the one worth trying on a card nobody would call suitable.
Passed the whole suite and kept every placeholder across four draws, in 2.9 GB of video memory.

Translation-specialised and light: 2.9 GB of video memory, the whole suite passed and four draws in four keeping their placeholders. An earlier single draw had dropped one at the end of a line, which is the sort of thing only repeated draws settle.
Passed the whole suite and kept every placeholder across four draws, in 3.2 GB of video memory — a third of what its download suggests.
The reference model's small sibling: same suite passed, four draws in four keeping their placeholders, in 3.9 GB of video memory instead of 6.1.
Passed the whole suite including the experimental source-language rule — one of only two here that does — and kept every placeholder across four draws, in 7.5 GB of video memory.
Passed the whole suite and kept every placeholder across four draws, but took 9.3 GB of video memory — well beyond what its 5.2 GB download suggests, and beyond an 8 GB card.

Not offered on purpose: it passes the whole suite, yet dropped a placeholder on one draw in four of the same line. Its 4B sibling held all four for the same job in a third of the memory, and a model that mangles a line now and then damages a game's text without ever announcing it.

A whole family rather than one model, so no size or figure is given here. Gemma has no separate system turn — it is merged into the conversation, which makes it more sensitive to how instructions are phrased.

Reasons before answering, so every line costs noticeably more time. Not offered for download either: the smaller build is a 14 GB download and the other 65 GB, both beyond the cards this tool is aimed at.
